title: From Preference Data to Personalization: Tracing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.21650v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We study sycophancy as inappropriate agreement: validating a claim, preference, or self-assessment when the context calls for correction, qualification, or resistance. We introduce a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, a persona-targeted evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes with controlled annotations for user openness and stakes. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. translated_title: 从偏好数据到个性化：追踪大语言模型中的谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 大语言模型中的谄媚行为通常被衡量为对用户的附和，然而当用户的主张是有效的、其偏好是真实的、或其经历值得认同时，附和可能是恰当的。本文将谄媚研究为一种不恰当的附和：即当情境需要纠正、限定或抵制时，仍然对某一主张、偏好或自我评估表示认可。作者引入了一个有效性感知的谄媚评分器，以及SycoDrift——一个面向人设的评估集，包含3,298个带有有效性标注的探针，并对用户的开放性和事情的利害程度进行了受控标注。研究利用这一框架分析了三种附和压力的来源：人类偏好数据、自动化评判器的规范设定以及上下文中的个性化。首先，在人类数据集（Chatbot Arena、HH-RLHF、Community Alignment）中，对认可性回答的偏好较弱，且集中在附和往往恰当的场景中；其次，在选定值、单模型实验中……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了有效性感知的谄媚评分器和包含3,298个有效性标注探针的SycoDrift评估集，将谄媚重新定义为“不当附和”而非简单的一致，并据此系统追踪了大语言模型附和压力的三个来源：人类偏好数据、自动评判器规范与上下文个性化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, an evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes, redefining sycophancy as inappropriate agreement rather than mere user-alignment, and systematically tracing three sources of agreement pressure in LLMs: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization.
